name: sprite2d
description: Pictures for entities: a sprite is one cell of an atlas drawn at the entity's Position, and an animation steps through consecutive cells. Tiles, characters, items and effects are all sprites.

components.name: Sprite
components.description: Draws one cell of an atlas centred on the entity's Position. atlas names an atlas of the game (game.json "atlases"); frame is the cell number, counted row by row from the top left. width and height are in world units, 0 meaning the cell's own size. Sprites with a higher layer are drawn over lower ones; at equal layers the older entity is drawn first. red, green, blue and alpha (0 to 255) tint and fade the picture; 255 leaves it as it is. pivot_x and pivot_y say which point of the picture sits on the Position: 0 is the left or top edge, 0.5 the middle (the default), 1 the right or bottom edge; they need a width and a height to have an effect. With screen, the Position and the size are pixels of the window and the camera does not move or zoom the sprite: that is how an interface stays put while the world scrolls. additive adds the picture's light to what is under it (glows, sparks, rays of light: black adds nothing); multiply darkens what is under it by the picture's colour (shadows, tints: white changes nothing); with neither it simply covers what is under it. A transform2d.Rotation turns the picture around its Position.

components.name: Parallax
components.description: Makes the entity's Sprite a plane at a distance: x and y say how much of the camera's movement it follows (1 moves with the world, 0.5 half as much, as a far plane does; 0 stays put on the screen, as the sky does; above 1 moves faster, as a plane nearer than the action does). The zoom applies to it as to the rest. With repeat_x the picture is drawn again side by side, every width, across the whole view: one picture makes an endless band (hills, clouds, a ground). Put the farthest planes on the lowest layers.

components.name: SpriteAnimation
components.description: Makes the entity's Sprite play the cells first_frame, first_frame + 1, ... for frame_count cells, each shown for ticks_per_frame simulation ticks. With looping it starts over; without, it stays on the last cell. elapsed counts the ticks played and is the animation's own state: leave it at 0, or set it to start part-way.

components.name: FrameBind
components.description: Chooses the Sprite's picture from a number of the game: every tick, the entity's own number field (written "module.Component.field", for example "slide_merge.Tile.value") gives the cell first_frame + n, where n is the number itself, or its base 2 logarithm rounded down (2 gives 1, 8 gives 3, 0 gives 0) with log2. frame_count, when more than 0, stops it on the last of that many cells. The colour of a tile from its value, a gauge, a state shown by a picture. A missing component leaves n at 0.

systems.name: animate
systems.description: Advances every SpriteAnimation by one tick and sets its Sprite's frame. It runs in the simulation, so an animation is the same on every run and every machine.

systems.name: draw
systems.description: Asks the renderer to draw every Sprite, lowest layer first. Presentation only: it never changes the simulation. The frame is ended by whoever runs the loop.

systems.name: bind_frame
systems.description: Sets the frame of every Sprite that has a FrameBind from the entity's own number.
